text: The passage repays attention to what is missing from it; for Sarah appears nowhere in Genesis 22, and the book reports her death in the verse immediately following the chapter. The scene says nothing directly, yet it implies that something in the household did not survive the mountain. After the event Abraham returns to the servants; of Isaac, at that return, no mention is made. The narration leaves the matter at the very point where a weaker story would have dwelt, and its silence means more than omission: Isaac is not mentioned.
